text: Among the MSCA-funded projects classified under inclusive education or special education, which ones collected their research data directly from large numbers of school students themselves, and how did their research designs differ?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocTitle IN ('inclusive education','special education') AND p.fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA%' ORDER BY p.id

reference_answer: Two of the six survivors did: IE2 (660607) and INCLUDed (101030992). IE2 ran its data collection inside schools - 'More than one thousand students across 35 classrooms took part, 25 teachers, administrators and district leaders' in Southern California, with data from two further European countries added during the first 24 months - and analysed it by combining advanced social network analysis with ethnographic methods to examine social interactions, friendships and peer relationships, with an emphasis on students identified as having special educational needs; its deliverables include a social network analysis toolkit for practitioners. INCLUDed collected data from a large nationally representative sample of 14-year-old lower-secondary students in Italy in order to develop, adapt and validate multifaceted measurement instruments for intercultural competence (IC) and for classroom cultural diversity climate (CCDC), the latter 'based on student perceptions of their learning environments', and then examined which culturally inclusive teaching approaches went with stronger IC. The designs differ in kind: IE2 is a school-based mixed network-and-ethnography study whose output is a practitioner toolkit, while INCLUDed is a large-scale quantitative instrument-development study whose output is validated measures plus evidence on teaching strategies.
notes: FILTER: purely structural - euroSciVoc leaf membership crossed with fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA%'; unchanged since the first draft. Both leaves pass the one-reading check: SELECT DISTINCT euroSciVocPath, euroSciVocTitle, COUNT(DISTINCT projectID) FROM euroscivoc WHERE euroSciVocPath ILIKE '%inclusive education%' OR euroSciVocPath ILIKE '%special education%' GROUP BY 1,2 returns exactly two rows, 'social sciences/educational sciences/inclusive education' (10 projects) and 'social sciences/educational sciences/special education' (10), each a leaf, so title reading = subtree reading. Union of the two leaves is 19 projects (660607 carries both tags); crossing with MSCA leaves 6 survivors. No text/topic predicate anywhere in filter_sql. TEXTUAL PREDICATE: the project's own research data were collected directly from school students, in large numbers. Each conjunct is stated in both gold texts. ADJUDICATION (exhaustive, S=6, every survivor read incl. workPerformed/finalResults): 660607 IE2 IN - 'Data collection from schools in Southern California has been completed. More than one thousand students across 35 classrooms took part, 25 teachers, administrators and district leaders'; 'data from two additional European countries have been collected during the first 24 months'. 101030992 INCLUDed IN - 'collected data from a large representative sample of lower-secondary students'; instrument for classroom cultural diversity climate 'based on student perceptions of their learning environments'; sample described in the objective as 'a large nationally representative sample of young people (14-year-olds) in a European country (i.e. Italy)'. 747083 MedLitRefYouth OUT - participants are not school students and are not numerous: '56 unaccompanied refugee children were interviewed', recruited 'By working with NGOs, volunteers and municipalities' in Italy and Sweden. 777720 CybSPEED OUT - no data collected from students: 'The grounds for sound experimental research have been laid, with some experiments already under way'; outputs are a theoretical framework, CPS models and Lattice Computing methods. 845783 ASSESSnet OUT - 'The data was principally collected by means of an online questionnaire and interviews with teachers involved in VM'; respondents are tertiary-level teachers. 101008184 xFORMAL OUT - work performed is scenario identification, a pathway editor, game mockups and feasibility tests of trails; no student data collection at all. DISCRIMINATION (unscoped pooled k=10 on the current question text) surfaced text-satisfying projects that fail the filter: 101018401 INCLUSION (ERC-ADG, euroSciVoc political economy|human migrations - 'We launched the Mitigation Study in the 2021-2022 academic year, covering over 20,000 students from 65 middle schools in Diyarbakir, Turkey ... collecting data from students via tablets'), 101004653 Inclusion4Schools (CSA, democracy|ethnology - 'A comprehensive survey was carried out ... targeting 1,358 schools'), 749068 GENSEG (MSCA fellowship, no inclusive/special-education tag - 'Using secondary data of 2235 adolescents from SOEP'). So the filter is load-bearing. TEXT LOAD-BEARING: no stored column records who a project's data came from or how its design was built; the filter alone returns six projects of which four are off-question. SCOPED RANKS (k=10, scope 6, current text): 101030992 lexical 1 / dense 1 / hybrid 1 / rerank 1; 660607 lexical 2 / dense 2 / hybrid 2 / rerank 2 - both gold top-2 in every condition, ahead of all four rejects. TERM_STYLE paraphrase: the textual half uses none of the gold texts' distinctive vocabulary ('social network analysis', 'friendship networks', 'special educational needs', 'intercultural competence', 'classroom cultural diversity climate', 'nationally representative sample'); the only verbatim overlap ('inclusive education' in IE2's title) sits in the scope half.

text: Among ERC Starting Grant projects whose abstract mentions autism, which ones carry out their experiments in a non-human species, and which species do they use?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT p.id FROM project p WHERE (p.objective ILIKE '%autis%' OR p.title ILIKE '%autis%') AND p.fundingScheme = 'ERC-STG' ORDER BY p.id

reference_answer: Nine of the 29 ERC Starting Grants whose abstract mentions autism run their experiments in a non-human species; the other 20 work with human participants, human cohorts or human data. Rodents dominate: THERAUTISM screens molecular targets and a gene-therapy vector in preclinical mouse models of ASD, REVERSEAUTISM pairs Slc7a5 and BCKDK mutant mice with human cerebral organoids, DisConn images the awake mouse and maps the mouse axonal connectome, SafeFate characterises Myt1l knockout mice alongside human induced neurons, and NEUROGOAL and MotivatedBehaviors both record from circuits in behaving mice. Three step outside rodents - HomeoBalanceExcInh dissects excitation/inhibition balance in Drosophila Kenyon cells, MultiSense records whole-brain activity in larval zebrafish, and Brain2Bee tests its dopamine model in the honey bee.
notes: Filter: fundingScheme = 'ERC-STG' plus the '%autis%' text condition over objective and title, which is what makes the survivor set enumerable (29 survivors). The question's anchor is worded to describe exactly what the filter reads - the project's own abstract - so a project whose only autism tie is in its published report (e.g. 637591 NEURAL AS, whose report mentions 'autistic spectrum disorders' while its abstract does not) is outside the question as well as outside the survivor set. At the runtime the structured half carries only fundingScheme; the topical half falls to retrieval (scoped.py whitelists no subject-matter column). Adjudication was exhaustive: all 29 survivor objectives read, plus workPerformed/finalResults for every IN and borderline case, plus a survivor-scoped SQL species sweep (mouse/mice, rat/rodent, zebrafish, Drosophila/flies, honey bee, monkey/macaque/primate/ferret/C. elegans over objective + report text). The adjudication test is whether the project's own text shows it carrying out experiments in a named non-human species. IN (9): 639489 HomeoBalanceExcInh - Drosophila Kenyon-cell circuit, 'allowing flies to learn to discriminate between different odours'; 677878 NEUROGOAL - two-photon imaging in 'foraging mice' and a mouse model of autism; 715508 REVERSEAUTISM - 'Employing a series of mouse models', plus human cerebral organoids; 715980 MultiSense - 'brain-wide response of larval zebrafish'; 757583 Brain2Bee - 'an animal model, the honey bee'; 802371 DisConn - 'recordings in the awake mouse', 'mouse axonal connectome'; 804710 SafeFate - 'new Myt1l knockout mouse models'; 851231 THERAUTISM - 'the most suitable and robust preclinical mouse models of ASD'; 949652 MotivatedBehaviors - 'I characterized in mice a novel circuit', mouse models of psychiatric disease. OUT (20): 636458 CogSoCoAGE, 676943 SLAB, 678286 CONTEXTVISION, 678733 CAASD, 679927 SYNAPLAST MR, 715824 POINTS, 716974 Becoming Social, 755816 AUTISMS, 801708 ANTICIPATE, 801715 PUPILTRAITS, 804881 NEUROEPIGENETHICS, 852570 CoCoFlex, 852885 INDIVISUAL, 853211 DEVCOM, 946228 DEFEND, 948545 TrackingMinds, 950010 FamilySleeps - human participants, human cohorts, human imaging/gaze/pupillometry data, algorithms or ethics work, with no species keyword anywhere in objective or report text; plus three that do experimental biology without ever showing an experiment in a named species - 716011 NANOGLU ('synaptic proteins endogenously expressed in neurons'), 950013 CERCODE ('models of early cerebellar disruptions'), and 803984 GIDE, whose only species word in the whole record is the abstract's closing CV clause 'my extensive training in viral and mouse genetic techniques' while all four report sections (lineage barcoding, single-cell transcriptomics, membrane-potential perturbation) name no organism. Discrimination counter-examples (satisfy the text, fail the ERC-STG filter): 899727 DUPDOWN (ERC-POC) 'brain organoids and in vivo models' for ASD; 660259 OPTOFRAX (MSCA-IF-EF-RI) 'Optopharmacological brain mapping of autism mouse models'; 845065 CANSAS (MSCA-IF) 'fMRI in rodents and humans' for autism subtypes; 700999 NMDARETT (MSCA-IF); 799164 ProTeAN (MSCA-IF-EF-RI); 844318 NeuroTick (MSCA-IF). term_style = paraphrase: the discriminating vocabulary ('non-human species', 'carry out their experiments') appears nowhere in the gold texts, which say Drosophila/flies, foraging mice, larval zebrafish, honey bee, awake mouse, Myt1l knockout mouse models; only the topical anchor is close to the survivors' shared wording, and it is the filter-side anchor, not the discriminator. Scoped retrievability: the drafter's own k=20 scoped pooled run placed 6 of the accepted members in some condition's top-20; the independent reviewer's re-measurement with differently worded scoped queries reached 9 of 10 and then 10 of 10, so the shortfall was a property of one query wording, not of the cell.
